question.text: Under which circumstances must a Regulated Entity NOT establish a business relationship with a customer?

answer.text: All three: where ownership or control arrangements prevent identifying Beneficial Owners; where there are anonymous, fictitious-name or undisclosed nominee accounts; and where the customer is a Shell Financial Institution
Where ownership or control arrangements prevent identifying the customer's Beneficial Owners
Where there are anonymous accounts or accounts in fictitious names
Where the customer is a Shell Financial Institution

explanation.text: The Logic: The IFSCA Guidelines state that a Regulated Entity shall not establish a business relationship where: (a) ownership or control arrangements prevent identification of the Beneficial Owners; (b) there are anonymous accounts, fictitious-name accounts, or undisclosed nominee accounts; or (c) the customer is a Shell Financial Institution. All three are absolute prohibitions. The Trap: Each single-circumstance distractor is correct on its own and may seem complete, but all three situations are independent prohibitions. There is no discretion or risk-based exception that allows the relationship to proceed in any of these cases, and no level of enhanced due diligence can overcome them. Note: Replaced the answer-randomization-fragile 'All of the above' wording with a standalone option that lists all three prohibited circumstances, and removed the cross-exam/pro-tip lines that were not source-grounded.
